study.design: cross-sectional environmental survey (isolates from a landfill leachate treatment station and receiving river)
study.region_city: Borj Chakir / Djebel Chekir landfill, south-west of Tunis; Oued El Attar river
study.environment: municipal solid waste landfill (receives some clinical waste) - leachate treatment pilot station and river receiving treated leachate
study.source_details: C6: 20 samples from different steps of the leachate treatment station (young leachate, permeate, raw leachate, concentrate, H2SO4 98% step, ultrafiltration) and from the Oued El Attar river receiving the treated leachate; C. tropicalis came from the river (n=13) and the H2SO4 98% step (n=3)
study.identification_method: CHROMagar Candida, morphology, API Candida / API 20C, MALDI-TOF MS (Bruker microflex)
study.susceptibility_method: amphotericin B disc diffusion on MHGBM agar (100 µg disc) and broth microdilution (RPMI 1640, protocol of Noumi et al.) for MIC/MFC
study.standard_document: CLSI/NCCLS cited for disc interpretation; non-standard protocol (Noumi et al.) for microdilution
study.breakpoint_type: author-defined (disc zones: R ≤9 mm, SDD 10–14 mm, S ≥15 mm); no MIC interpretation
study.comments: Only amphotericin B tested; no azoles. Text says 17 C. tropicalis (46.94%) but Table 1 lists 16 isolates (M2, M5, M7, M16, M20, M21, M24, M25, M36, M42, M43, M45, M46, M47, M56, M57); data are extracted from the table. Individual MICs and zone diameters are reported per isolate. The text's summary of categories (12 R, 13 S, 14 SDD) contradicts the zone cut-offs and the table; the table interpretation is used. The disc method and breakpoints are non-standard; no collection dates.

study.design: laboratory method-comparison study with clinical bloodstream isolates
study.region_city: Houston, Texas (testing laboratory); isolates from a US collection
study.environment: mycology research laboratory; isolates randomly selected from a US bloodstream-isolate collection
study.susceptibility_method: CLSI broth microdilution, E-test and disc diffusion (posaconazole 5 µg discs from Oxoid and BD) on Mueller-Hinton + 2% glucose + methylene blue
study.breakpoint_type: author-defined arbitrary breakpoint (≤1 µg/mL susceptible) used only for agreement; no species-level categorisation reported
study.comments: Only posaconazole tested. MIC50, MIC90 and range are reported per species, but there are no S/R counts per species; the agreement rates are percentages. For C. tropicalis, the ET/MD concordance was 39.0% at 24 h and 70.7% at 48 h, and the categorical agreement was 97.6% and 85.4%. Discordance was attributed to trailing growth. Three of 4 very major errors were C. tropicalis isolates. No collection dates.

study.design: cross-sectional (laboratory-based, retrospective collection of clinical isolates)
study.environment: university hospital microbiology laboratory (tertiary hospital; 75.6% of isolates from ICUs)
study.source_details: C1: non-albicans Candida from clinical samples - blood (54), urine (25), wound (2), catheter (1); not stratified by species
study.identification_method: BD Phoenix Yeast ID panel + ITS1-ITS4 rDNA Sanger sequencing (reference)
study.standard_version: E.Def 7.3.1 / 7.3.2; breakpoint table version not stated
study.comments: The stem title ('Molecular typing') differs from the published title. The study used DNA sequencing for identification only, with no strain typing. There were 30 C. tropicalis by sequencing (26 by Phoenix), and susceptibility data use the sequencing-based species (Table 4, n=30). Resistance counts for C. tropicalis are in the text. Counts for S and I are not reported. Six C. tropicalis isolates were cross-resistant to at least 2 triazoles. Sample sources are not given per species. The EUCAST breakpoint version is not identified.

clade4.note: ITS sequencing used for species identification only; no MLST/typing

study.environment: tertiary hospital (Sir J.J. Group of Hospitals / Grant Medical College)
study.source_details: C1: oral pseudomembranous plaques (scrapings) of an AIDS patient
study.population: 34-year-old man with AIDS (CD4 40 cells/µL) and disseminated cryptococcosis
study.identification_method: germ tube, cornmeal-Tween 80 morphology, Vitek-32 and API 20C AUX
study.azole_exposure: documented prior fluconazole (and amphotericin B) treatment
study.comments: Single isolate; no MIC values reported. The report states only that 'fluconazole resistance to C. tropicalis only' was found among fluconazole, ketoconazole, clotrimazole, posaconazole and amphotericin B, so susceptibility to the other agents is implied. The resistance mechanisms (ERG11, efflux) are discussed from the literature only and were not tested. The patient died on day 3.

study.environment: obstetrics and gynaecology clinics, Authority Al-Gumhorri Hospital Hajjah
study.source_details: C1: vaginal swabs from 396 symptomatic pregnant women
study.population: pregnant women with symptoms of vaginitis (17–44 years)
study.identification_method: SDA culture, HiCrome chromogenic agar, germ tube, API 20C AUX
study.susceptibility_method: disc diffusion (Kirby-Bauer) on Mueller-Hinton + 2% glucose + methylene blue (HiMedia discs)
study.standard_document: CLSI (2021) Performance standards for antimicrobial susceptibility testing (M100, 31st ed., as cited)
study.azole_exposure: not stated (women on current antimicrobial treatment excluded; recurrent infection in 70.5%)
study.comments: The cited CLSI document is the antibacterial M100. The zone breakpoints (e.g. fluconazole S ≥39 mm, R ≤29 mm) do not match CLSI M44/M60 and give no intermediate category, so S + R = n. No MICs are reported. The miconazole R percentage for C. tropicalis is printed as 19.6%, but 8/27 = 29.6% (counts used). Identification is phenotypic only.

clade4.note: No genotyping performed (stated as a limitation)

study.design: retrospective cohort / laboratory-based surveillance of candidaemia
study.environment: tertiary regional hospital (Hospital Base Valdivia, 505 beds, adult and paediatric ICUs)
study.source_details: C1: blood cultures (first episode per patient)
study.population: hospitalised patients with candidaemia (ages 1–84 years; 59.3% >65 years)
study.identification_method: CHROMagar Candida, Tween 80 rice agar microculture, carbohydrate assimilation, ID-32C for difficult isolates; RAPD for C. parapsilosis complex only
study.susceptibility_method: disc diffusion with Neo-Sensitabs tablets (Rosco) on MH + 2% glucose + methylene blue
study.breakpoint_type: manufacturer-defined zone breakpoints (Rosco) (FLC S ≥19, I 15–18, R ≤14 mm; VOR S ≥17, I 14–16, R ≤13 mm)

study.comments: Itraconazole results appear in Table 3, but itraconazole is not listed in the methods. The authors state that disc diffusion is validated only for fluconazole and voriconazole. The amphotericin B, caspofungin and itraconazole categories rely on manufacturer criteria. Very small number of C. tropicalis (n=4). Collection period March 2009–August 2011.

study.environment: anaesthesiology intensive care unit of a tertiary university hospital (Dokuz Eylül University)
study.source_details: C1: clinical infection sites of ICU patients; C. tropicalis from urine (11) and catheter (1)
study.population: anaesthesiology ICU patients (56 of 178 patients yielded Candida)
study.infection_type: non-invasive (mostly urinary) with one catheter isolate
study.identification_method: germ tube, cornmeal-Tween 80 morphology, CHROMagar Candida, API 20C AUX
study.comments: Individual MICs and isolation dates are reported per isolate (Table 1; February 2002–March 2003). Four C. tropicalis isolates were fluconazole SDD (16–32 µg/mL) and none were resistant. Amphotericin B was 'susceptible' per the authors (M27-A2 has no formal amphotericin B breakpoint). RAPD typing: 9 groups at SAB ≥0.90. CT-1 and CT-2 came from the same patient but were unrelated. Group membership is shown only in the dendrogram (Fig. 7), so counts per group could not be extracted.
